cases.title: Nobel Ti-Base Maxillary Full-Arch Provisional | Digital Design & Laboratory Try-In
cases.technicalSummary: A maxillary full-arch provisional restoration designed and finished on Nobel Ti-bases for seating, emergence-profile and occlusal verification before the definitive prosthesis.
cases.material: Provisional PMMA/resin with characterized pink gingiva and bonded Nobel Ti-bases

cases.challenge: The provisional had to coordinate full-arch seating, screw-access position, emergence contours and occlusion while maintaining natural tooth proportions and gingival support. Accurate Ti-base integration was essential for a stable laboratory try-in.
cases.planning: The maxillary arch was planned digitally around the supplied implant positions and Nobel Ti-base interfaces. Tooth setup, pink gingival volume, screw-channel access and opposing-arch contacts were reviewed together before manufacturing.
cases.technicalReview: QC priorities: confirm complete seating of every Ti-base interface, passive fit on the verified model, clean screw-channel access, bonding-surface control, full-arch occlusion and polished tissue-contact areas. The provisional stage allows clinical verification before the definitive restoration.
cases.technicalOutcome: The completed provisional demonstrated stable seating on the model, accessible screw channels, balanced anterior proportions and continuous gingival contouring, providing a practical verification stage before the definitive restoration.
cases.clinicalNotes: Laboratory documentation of a provisional restoration. Final seating, passivity, screw torque, tissue pressure and occlusion must be verified clinically by the treating dentist.
cases.workflow: Model and implant-component review → digital full-arch design → provisional resin manufacture → Nobel Ti-base bonding → gingival characterization and finishing → articulated model try-in → screw-access and occlusal quality control.

cases.title: Maxillary Esthetic Rehabilitation | Restoring Anterior Proportion & Smile Harmony
cases.technicalSummary: This case documents the initial maxillary esthetic condition, completed restorations on the working model, and a digital smile-design preview. The focus is anterior proportion, individual tooth morphology, shade harmony, and cervical transitions. The digital proposal is not a confirmed clinical result; material, restoration count, final clinical findings, and public-display consent remain to be confirmed.
cases.summary:
This case documents maxillary esthetic rehabilitation through initial clinical photographs, laboratory photographs of restorations on a working model, and a digital smile-design comparison. The supplied records illustrate the transition from irregular anterior proportions and uneven coloration to a coordinated restorative arrangement on the model.

The laboratory photographs show balanced tooth proportions, differentiated facial contours, a visually harmonious shade progression, and cervical transitions adjacent to the simulated gingiva. These are laboratory observations, not evidence of a final intraoral outcome. The video presents a digital esthetic proposal rather than verified clinical delivery.

coverImage.caption: Frontal laboratory view of maxillary restorations on the working model, documenting anterior proportions, individualized facial morphology, visual shade harmony, and cervical transitions.
coverImage.altText: Frontal view of completed maxillary esthetic restorations on the working model

cases.caseOverview:
This case documents maxillary esthetic rehabilitation through initial clinical photographs, laboratory photographs of restorations on a working model, and a digital smile-design comparison. The supplied records illustrate the transition from irregular anterior proportions and uneven coloration to a coordinated restorative arrangement on the model.

The laboratory photographs show balanced tooth proportions, differentiated facial contours, a visually harmonious shade progression, and cervical transitions adjacent to the simulated gingiva. These are laboratory observations, not evidence of a final intraoral outcome. The video presents a digital esthetic proposal rather than verified clinical delivery.
cases.challenge:
Esthetic Challenges

The initial records show anterior color differences, irregular facial morphology, visible interdental spaces, uneven incisal edges, and localized incisal defects. The esthetic challenge is to coordinate apparent tooth proportions, alignment, interproximal transitions, and shade harmony without making the anterior segment appear uniformly shaped or artificial. The cause of the visible defects and the clinical treatment plan are not documented.
cases.planning:
Initial Clinical Condition

The pre-treatment smile photograph and retracted intraoral view show uneven anterior coloration, irregular tooth contours, visible spacing, and incisal irregularities or defects. No diagnosis, preparation design, material selection, or restoration count is inferred from these images.

Laboratory Approach

The documented laboratory review focuses on anterior proportion, individual tooth character, central-to-lateral-to-canine progression, proximal transitions, cervical contours, and the relationship to the opposing working model. Facial and bilateral oblique views provide complementary references for reviewing the same restoration. Clinical contact strength, dynamic occlusion, and long-term performance require separate clinical confirmation.
cases.technicalReview:
Restoration Morphology

The restorations on the working model display individualized facial convexity, line angles, incisal outline, and a coordinated anterior progression. The photographs show a natural-looking shade distribution and smooth cervical transitions adjacent to the model's simulated gingiva. Apparent color in photographs is not a verified shade specification.

Quality Control

The supplied frontal and bilateral views support visual review of tooth proportions, surface morphology, proximal transitions, cervical contours, arch continuity, and the relationship to the opposing model. They do not establish internal fit, measured contact strength, dynamic occlusion, or an intraoral outcome.
cases.cadDesign:
Digital Smile Design Preview

The supplied screen recording compares the initial smile photograph with a digital esthetic proposal. It is a planning visualization, not a photograph or video of the delivered clinical restoration. Software identity, final design approval, and clinical correspondence have not been confirmed.
cases.finalRestoration:
Restoration Morphology

Completed maxillary restorations are shown on the working model from frontal and bilateral oblique perspectives. The views document anterior proportion, facial contour, line-angle definition, individual tooth character, visual shade harmony, and cervical transitions. No material, tooth count, or clinical delivery outcome is claimed.
cases.qc:
Quality Control

The available photographs document visual review of facial contours, proximal transitions, cervical emergence, arch continuity, and the relationship to the opposing working model. Internal fit, contact pressure, dynamic occlusion, and clinical tissue response cannot be established from these records alone.
cases.technicalOutcome: Documentation currently supports a laboratory model review and a digital smile-design proposal. Final clinical results have not been supplied or verified. The case remains a private draft pending public-display authorization, de-identification of visible model text, and confirmation of the missing clinical and material information.
cases.clinicalNotes:
Publication Hold / Pending Confirmation

Public-display authorization for the patient photographs and video has not been confirmed. Eye masking alone does not establish de-identification. One lateral model photograph contains visible identifying text; a separate redacted presentation copy is required before any public use. Original files must remain unchanged.

Pending clinical information: restoration material, exact restoration count and tooth positions, prescribed shade, treatment and preparation details, clinician approval, and final clinical seating photographs or findings. The digital smile-design preview must not be labeled as a final clinical result.

cases.title: Six Ultra-Thin Anterior Veneers | Digital Esthetic Planning & Precision Verification
cases.technicalSummary: A six-unit maxillary anterior veneer case developed through digital esthetic planning, conservative ceramic contours, controlled restoration thickness, and working-model verification.
cases.restorationType: Six maxillary anterior ultra-thin ceramic veneers
cases.challenge: The objective was to design six ultra-thin veneers for the maxillary anterior segment while maintaining balanced tooth proportions, a natural progression in width and length, and an intentional incisal relationship. The restorations were evaluated as one coordinated anterior composition rather than as isolated units.
cases.planning: Digital references were used to evaluate the facial midline, tooth width-to-length relationships, bilateral balance, and incisal curvature. The central incisors, lateral incisors, and canines were planned together while preserving individual morphology and natural variation.
cases.technicalReview: Six maxillary anterior ultra-thin ceramic veneers. The workflow focused on digital esthetic references, coordinated anterior morphology, controlled restoration volume, mechanical thickness checking, and final working-model evaluation. Exact ceramic system, shade, software package, and measured thickness values were not supplied.
cases.technicalOutcome: The six-unit veneer case was reviewed for morphology, surface quality, controlled thickness, seating, proximal relationships, and integration with the working model before delivery. The image set documents selected planning, fabrication, thickness-control, and model-verification steps.
cases.clinicalNotes: This is a laboratory workflow case. The supplied images document digital planning, fabrication, and model-based evaluation only. They do not represent an intraoral before-and-after result, and clinical bonding outcomes are not documented.
cases.workflow: Following digital planning, the ceramic veneers were fabricated with a conservative external profile. Each restoration was reviewed for contour, proximal relationship, surface morphology, and optical consistency. A mechanical gauge was used to check restoration thickness, followed by model evaluation from frontal, lateral, and occlusal perspectives.

cases.title: Posterior Implant Crown with Custom Zirconia Abutment
cases.technicalSummary: Custom zirconia abutment on a titanium base with a full-contour zirconia crown. Reviewed for emergence profile, marginal adaptation, proximal contacts, occlusion and final contour.
cases.restorationType: Custom Zirconia Abutment + Full-Contour Zirconia Crown
cases.material: Custom zirconia abutment on a titanium base + full-contour zirconia crown
cases.challenge: The case required a customized emergence profile and a precise transition between the implant abutment and the posterior crown.
cases.planning: The abutment and crown were planned as a coordinated restorative unit, with attention to restorative space, crown contour, occlusal anatomy and the implant component interface.
cases.technicalReview: Reviewed restorative space, implant component interface, abutment height, emergence profile, crown contour, proximal contacts and occlusal anatomy on the working model.
cases.technicalOutcome: The completed restoration showed a clean emergence profile, natural posterior anatomy and a consistent crown-to-abutment relationship on the working model.
cases.workflow: The workflow included digital design, custom zirconia abutment fabrication on a titanium base, full-contour zirconia crown production and model-based verification.
